wants.topic: Absurd and strangely human daily life in ancient civilizations
wants.evidence: Nils History's 'Ancient Babylon Was Weirder Than You Think' (vsNormal 2.74) and 'The First Civilization in the World Was Rather Strange' (vsNormal 1.63), where top comments focus heavily on ancient gas station equivalents, quirky omens, and human pit burials.

wants.topic: Authentic human-narrated history as an alternative to AI voiceovers
wants.evidence: Nils History including '(No AI)' in titles and comments like 'Dude, awesome narration... in the age of AI slop, this kind of quality is pure gold' and praise for human storytelling.

wants.topic: Behind-the-scenes institutional scandals, terrible ideas, and cover-ups
wants.evidence: VICE Vault's 'Wrestling's Worst Idea Ever: Brawl For All' (vsNormal 2.47) and 'Jimmy Snuka & The Death of Nancy Argentino' (vsNormal 1.89) generating massive engagement around corrupt authority figures and disastrous administrative decisions.

wants.topic: Origins and lesser-known details of Ancient World Wonders and lost sites
wants.evidence: Nils History's 'The First Wonders of the World Were Rather Strange' (vsNormal 1.98) with comments explicitly asking for Part 2 and requesting coverage of the Great Library of Alexandria.

gaps: High-quality human narrative explainers on ancient daily life and weird laws without relying on AI voiceovers or stock footage slop.
Detailed breakdowns of forgotten ancient monuments and intellectual hubs (e.g., Library of Alexandria) beyond the standard Seven Wonders list.
Geopolitical and historical breakdown of how systemic institutional cover-ups were executed in real time.
saturated: Generic AI-generated voiceover history summaries with visual stock footage.
Superficial celebrity-focused tech or luxury showcases without deep narrative friction.
Dry, textbook-style chronological lists of battles and royal successions devoid of human quirks or strangeness.
